Keys.Table: Show or hide the Duel Table
Keys.TableHint: Shows or hides the A Single Moment table.

Error.Phase: MR · Un momento único: phase “{phase}” failed. Foundry keeps working; check the diagnostic.

Settings.OpenOnStartHint: In window mode, opens the Table when the world loads. In full screen the Table always shows on login unless you hid it. A personal setting.
Settings.TableModeHint: Full screen: the Table covers the whole screen over the scene and can be hidden with the eye, the pill or the shortcut. Window: the Duel Table in a window. A personal setting.

Game.NoDoc: There is no game yet. Ask the GM to enter the world once.
Game.WaitGM: The game is prepared when the GM first enters the world.
Game.NewConfirm: This erases the current game (chapters, advantages, hate and scars). Seats are kept. Continue?

Counter.advHint: Spent in the Grand Finale: one per attack and one per extra die.
Counter.hateHint: Each point is a die rolled when dealing with hate. It breaks ties at the end.
Counter.scarHint: Whoever has more scars loses if nobody lands the mortal blow.

Table.Hide: Hide the Table and see only the scene

Chapter.Label: Chapter {n} of {total}
Chapter.Title: Chapter {n}
Chapter.YouAreActive: You are the active player: you act as Game Master for this chapter.
Chapter.ActiveIs: {name} is the active player and acts as Game Master.
Chapter.ActiveDecides: {name} has the last word on every decision.

Setup.Title: The opening scene
Setup.Name: Character name
Setup.IntroHint: “My name is… I am a member of the clan… This is my story.”
Setup.First: Goes first: whoever most recently watched a martial arts film
Setup.PlannedHint: Three for a short game, five for a standard one. You can change it at any time.
Setup.ChooseVirtue: Choose the virtue of the story
Setup.StartHint: The scene is declared. Now you tell, in flashbacks, how you came to be here.
Setup.NeedBoth: Both seats must be taken to begin.

Decl.eraHint: When the story happens: the season, maybe the year. Also choose the table's weather.
Decl.placeHint: The location, which may also hint at the technology level or the state of the surroundings.
Decl.span: It has taken us… to reach this moment.
Decl.spanHint: The time the whole story spans. It can be epic: more than a generation.
Decl.storyHint: Choose a virtue. It takes priority over the others throughout all chapters.

Between.Title: Chapter {n} closed
Between.Reached: You have reached the agreed number of chapters. You may deal with hate or keep telling.

Step1.Hint: Each player draws a virtue from the six left and the active player picks one for the chapter. Or keeps the story's virtue.

Step2.Hint: There are three key themes and all three must be played before the end. Starting a chapter with a key theme gives the active player two advantages.

Step3.Hint: The active player may introduce a key character. Whoever introduces them plays them in every later scene.
Step3.Name: Character name

Step4.Hint: {name} runs the scene. If a decision favours their samurai, the other player receives a choice marker; if it favours the other, they receive it.

Pool.Rule: The marker goes to the other player: whoever receives markers will have more dice in the climax, at the cost of what the story concedes.

Step5.Hint: Each player trades markers for dice. You may add extra dice (each gives a scar) and award two dice to whoever best embodied the virtue. Nobody goes past seven.

Climax.ExtraHint: Each extra die gives a scar
Climax.ConsonanceHint: Together you choose who best embodied the virtue: they get two dice. If you disagree, nobody does.
Climax.RivalNotReady: The other player is not ready yet.
Climax.TieText: Stalemate: each gains advantages equal to their markers and hate equal to the rival's, and the active player gains a scar.

Step6.Narrate: {name} narrates the end of the chapter and must respect the theme, at least as far as the active player is concerned.
Step6.NarrateTie: On a stalemate, {name} narrates the end in a neutral, direct way.

Hate.Title: Dealing with hate
Hate.Intro: Each samurai decides separately what to do with their hate before the Grand Finale.
Hate.Note: What your samurai does behind the other's back
Hate.NoteHint: The more dramatic the better. It may hurt people the rival cared about.
Hate.SurrenderHint: Roll all your hate dice: evens are advantages, odds are scars.
Hate.EscapeHint: Only with more than {n} hate. Discard scars equal to half your hate, rounded down. It gives no advantages and does not erase hate.
Hate.Keep: Keep the hate as it is
Hate.RollHint: You roll all {n} hate dice together. Evens are advantages; odds are scars.

Final.Title: The Grand Finale
Final.WhyHate: Whoever has more hate attacks first.
Final.WhyAdv: Tied on hate: whoever has more advantages attacks first.
Final.WhyScar: Tied on advantages: whoever has more scars attacks first.
Final.WhyFirst: All tied: whoever declared first attacks.
Final.RespondHint: How you defend against that move.
Final.SpendAtt: Attacking costs one advantage (one die). You may spend up to two more for extra dice.
Final.SpendDef: Defending is free (one die). You may spend up to two advantages for extra dice.
Final.HighestWins: Dice are not added: the highest die wins. The attacker must beat the defender.
Final.Clash: The swords clash. Blind bet: whoever bets more advantages wins.
Final.BetLocked: Bet locked. Both are revealed at once.
Final.BetHint: You may bet zero. Advantages bet are spent. If you bet the same, nobody takes a scar.
Final.Won: {name} wins the exchange and the other takes a scar.
Final.NoWinner: Nobody wins: the clash breaks and the fight goes on.
Final.MortalText: {att} lunges for the final blow against {def}.
Final.MortalRule: One die each, unmodified. If the attacker beats the defender, all their advantages become scars for the rival. A tie fails.

by.hate: Scars tied: whoever gathered less hate triumphs

Epilogue.Title: Epilogue
Epilogue.Triumph: The victor tells what happened right after
Epilogue.Defeated: The defeated adds something (dramatic, favouring the victor)
Epilogue.Hint: Write your part of the epilogue.

Warn.reserveLeft: There are still markers in the reserve. You may continue, but normally all seven are dealt.
Warn.themesPending: Key themes are still unplayed. The book asks for all three before the Grand Finale.

Chronicle.Empty: The Chronicle appears as soon as the first chapter closes.
Chronicle.Heading: Chronicle of {a} and {b}
Chronicle.Intro: My name is {name}. I am a member of the clan {clan}. This is my story.

Hate.surrender: {name} surrendered to hate: {adv} advantages and {scar} scars.

Chronicle.Totals: {a}: {aa} advantages, {ah} hate, {as} scars. {b}: {ba} advantages, {bh} hate, {bs} scars.
Chronicle.Credit: Based on “One Single Moment” (Un momento único), by Tobie Abad (The Hills Press, Spanish translation by Víctor Romero), CC BY 4.0. Foundry VTT system: MR · Un momento único, by Manu Romera. Virtue texts adapted and condensed.

Welcome.Title: MR · Un momento único
Welcome.Body: Two samurai, a frozen duel and the story of how they got there. Both of you, take a seat at the Duel Table.

Safety.Intro: Pause, Veil or X-Card: they alert the whole table at once, without saying who pressed them.
Safety.PauseText: The game stops for a moment.
Safety.VeilHint: Tell it without going into detail.
Safety.VeilText: We pass over this, without detail.
Safety.XHint: Not this. It is skipped, no questions asked.
Safety.XText: That stays out of the story. We continue another way.
Safety.Anonymous: Nobody will know who triggered it; the X-Card is not recorded anywhere.
Safety.Topics: Before you begin, talk about lines and veils: ritual suicide, violence against family and a duel to the death can be hard themes.

Access.Title: Accessibility and reading
Access.Intro: Personal settings: they only affect this system's windows and only in your browser.
Access.wideSpacingHint: More room between lines and letters.
Access.reducedMotionHint: No animations or brush strokes being drawn.
Access.reducedEffectsHint: No bleeding ink, no cinema bars.
Access.musicHint: A very sparse koto at key moments.
Access.darkModeHint: Everything dark: backgrounds, paper, cards and dice. No bright colours to dazzle.

Diagnostic.Title: Diagnostic
Diagnostic.Hint: A copyable report of the system's state, in case something fails.
Diagnostic.Problems: There are problems; copy the report and send it.

Err.wrongPhase: That cannot be done in this phase of the game.
Err.needNames: Both samurai need a name and a clan.
Err.needVirtue: Choose a virtue to close the declarations.
Err.drawing: Virtues are already on the table.
Err.badVirtue: That virtue is not on the table.
Err.badTheme: That theme has already been played.
Err.badCharacter: That key character is already in the story.
Err.locked: You are both ready: the dice are fixed.
Err.notReady: You both must be ready to roll.
Err.badDice: The dice do not match what was expected.
Err.cannotEscape: You can only escape hate if it is above ten.
Err.noHate: You have no hate to deal with.
Err.notEnoughAdvantages: You do not have enough advantages left.

Fix.Title: Fix by hand
Fix.Intro: To repair a mistake: raise or lower whatever the game spent or dealt on its own. While this is on, each player's counters (Advantages, Hate and Scars) show − and + next to them. Either player can do it and everything is recorded.
Fix.PoolHint: Move a marker between the reserve and a player. Only before the climax dice are rolled.
Fix.PoolLess: Return one of {name}'s markers to the reserve
Fix.ThemesHint: Mark a theme as played or put it back. The advantages it gave are fixed on the player's counter.
Fix.VirtuesHint: Move a virtue between the deck and the discard. The story's virtue, the chapter's and any on the table are left alone.
Fix.PlannedHint: How many chapters will be played
